scope: Run two independent PSCAD cold starts for a balanced resistive-load island with two autonomous fixed-amplitude averaged sources. Observe active-power sharing with unequal droop slopes after a load increase.

motivation.title: Droop Control-Based Dispatch of an Islanded Microgrid with Multiple Grid-Forming Sources
motivation.role: Published hardware study of independent primary droop. The fixture here follows the project's Case 37 and uses fresh native waveforms.

reference.basis: Use the proven Case 37 installed-master source, feeder, load and clock pattern. The phasor and continuous ODE screens size the observation windows and provide expected operating levels.

fixture.topology: Each phase has two ideal controlled phase-to-ground sources, each over its own series R–L branch to one grounded-Y PCC/load. Three identical phases share the ground. One additional Y resistor per phase connects on the programmed load row.
fixture.conventions: Source and PCC voltages are phase-to-neutral. Feeder currents are positive toward the PCC. Load currents are positive toward ground. Each station uses three solved PCC voltage-current products for total watts.

timing.row_semantics: Record every electrical row, including exactly zero and 0.6 s. Use right-endpoint switching at 0.300 s. Compute settled statistics over the half-open windows.

controller.rules: Start with zero applied amplitude and angle, zero feeder currents and each filter at its reference. At positive row k use the stored phase of each source. After solving the row, update each discrete power filter by backward Euler from its own PCC watts, apply f=60-m(P_filtered-P_ref), and advance its own unwrapped angle by 2*pi*h*f for the next row.

native.runtime: Independent cold starts. Retain native INF/OUT and compiled circuit, pre-run admission and owned completion for each grid. Disable network switching interpolation and chatter handling.

audit_notes: Reconstruct all six source voltages and both stations' separate power, filter, frequency and phase recurrences using the original solved rows. Validate PCC current and watts conservation, each load law, six original trapezoidal feeder intervals, and full-network interval energy using midpoint voltage and current.
Report the unchanged angle and reactor history semantics at the load edge and the measured power dip. The original time and phase origins are authoritative.

Compare exactly coincident rows across electrical grids. Compare every row with full-trace bounds and use the tighter voltage/current bounds beyond a fixed ±0.5 ms around the load edge. Compare each station’s own window watt and frequency means.

At a common settled frequency with matched m times P_ref, the incremental active powers are inversely proportional to droop slopes. The continuous screen predicts roughly 239.37 W versus 119.67 W with finite oscillatory residuals. A public numerical candidate requires a separately frozen acceptance protocol.
